idiom_name: class X implements Target holding the incompatible service
implementation_notes: Structural typing means a TypeScript adapter only has to have the right shape, and an explicit `implements Target` adds the compile-time check that it does; the adapter holds the incompatible service and translates its members. Where the target is a single operation or the mismatch is between data shapes, a plain function - or a generic Adapter<TSource, TTarget> - is idiomatic and cheaper than a class. Types are erased at run time, so data crossing a trust boundary must be validated or narrowed inside the adapter (assertion functions or a schema parser) rather than trusted because it was cast.
pitfalls: `as` casts silence the checker: an adapter full of type assertions gives no guarantee that the runtime value has the declared shape.
Types disappear at run time, so optional or union fields arriving as JSON can still be null; validate where data enters the adapter.
Structural typing lets an unmapped member accidentally satisfy a wider interface - declare narrow target interfaces and use `implements` to catch drift.
Returning the API's own types from the adapter leaks the vendor shape back to callers; map into your own DTO types.

variants.name: Mapper function between shapes
variants.implementation_notes: When what differs are data shapes rather than behavioural objects, the adapter is a pure function from the source type to the target type (or a generic Adapter<TSource, TTarget>); it composes with map/filter pipelines, is trivial to test, and carries no state. Choose a class when the target owns behaviour, has several operations, or needs dependencies of its own; choose the mapper when the job is a field-by-field translation.
pitfalls: A mapper that silently drops fields loses data when the source schema grows; keep the mapping exhaustive and test it.
Pure mappers do not validate: if the source is untrusted, parse and narrow before mapping.
Mapping deep object graphs per request is expensive when the adapter sits on a hot path - cache or stream instead.
